plain: Allowed by, or in line with, a country's constitution

webster.text: Bred or inherent in the constitution, or in the natural frame of body or mind; as a constitutional infirmity; constitutional ardor or dulness.

more.text: Consistent with the constitution; authorized by the constitution or fundamental rules of a government; legal.
Relating to the constitution; as a constitutional doubt.

example.quote: At present, I shall only remark, that it is difficult to conceive how the state legislatures can, in any case, hold a check over the general legislature, in a constitutional way.
example.cite: Brutus X, New York Journal, Jan. 24, 1788
